About this program
Earth Sciences and Environmental Sustainability, Doctor of Philosophy
Advance scientific understanding of the Earth while addressing complex environmental challenges through innovative research. Explore topics ranging from geology and hydrology to climate change, biodiversity, and sustainability.
Explore our changing planet
The biggest questions about our planet span many scientific disciplines. In this doctoral program, you'll explore topics ranging from geology and earth systems to climate, ecosystems, and the relationships between people and the environment while developing the research skills to investigate complex scientific questions. Whether you're studying how the Earth functions or addressing environmental challenges, you'll design, conduct, and communicate original research that aligns with your interests and career goals.
The program's interdisciplinary approach encourages collaboration across the earth, environmental, biological, and social sciences, helping you examine complex questions from multiple perspectives. Through hands-on research, collaboration with faculty, and access to the diverse landscapes of the Southwest, you'll contribute new knowledge while preparing for careers in academia, government, industry, nonprofit organizations, and research institutions.
Customize your doctoral experience through one of four emphasis areas. Whether you're interested in environmental change, earth processes, ecological systems, conservation, or the relationship between people and the environment, you'll find opportunities to pursue meaningful research aligned with your goals.
Climate and Environmental Change - study climate systems and environmental change while exploring their impacts on ecosystems, water resources, and the communities and ecosystems.
Earth Systems - explore the geological, hydrological, and environmental processes that shape our planet and influence natural resources, hazards, and sustainability.
Ecology, Evolution and Conservation Biology - investigate ecological and evolutionary processes while developing solutions to conservation and biodiversity challenges.
Environment and Society - examine the relationships between people and the environment through environmental policy, resource management, sustainability, and social systems.
Learn from the landscape
Study in a program that combines individualized mentorship with the flexibility to shape your research around your interests and career goals. Working closely with faculty, you'll develop expertise in your chosen area while collaborating across disciplines when your research calls for multiple perspectives.
As a student at NAU, you'll learn in one of the nation's most dynamic natural laboratories. From forests, mountains, watersheds, and canyons to deserts, Tribal lands, and growing communities, the Southwest provides exceptional opportunities for place-based research. You'll gain hands-on experience through fieldwork, data collection, laboratory analysis, and collaboration with faculty and research teams. With four emphasis areas spanning earth systems, climate and environmental change, ecology and conservation, and environment and society, you can tailor your doctoral experience to your research interests and career goals.
Discovery with purpose
As a graduate of this program, you'll be prepared to lead research, inform decision-making, and develop solutions to complex environmental challenges. Alumni pursue careers in academia, research institutions, environmental consulting, industry, nonprofit organizations, and government agencies at the federal, state, Tribal, and local levels. Whether your goal is advancing scientific knowledge, shaping environmental policy, managing natural resources, or supporting sustainable communities, you'll graduate with the expertise to make a meaningful impact.
Pursue questions that matter
How has our planet changed over time? What processes shape the Earth beneath our feet? How do ecosystems respond to environmental change? What policies support sustainable resource management? As a doctoral student, you'll explore questions like these while conducting original research that advances our understanding of the Earth, environment, and society. Your research might examine geological processes, hydrology, climate change, biodiversity and conservation, environmental policy, sustainability, or the connections between human and natural systems. With research opportunities spanning the earth, environmental, biological, and social sciences, you'll have the flexibility to pursue questions that align with your interests while contributing knowledge that informs science, policy, and natural resource management.
Graduate contact
Before applying, reach out to faculty whose research interests align with your own. A thoughtful introduction can help you learn more about research opportunities and potential mentorship. For general questions, contact the School of Earth and Sustainability at SES.Admin@nau.edu.
